name: Teke Teke
description: A Japanese urban-legend onryō: the spirit of a young woman or schoolgirl bisected by a train who travels on her hands or elbows, making a 'teke-teke' scratching sound, and bisects those she catches.
full_description: Teke Teke (テケテケ) is a Japanese urban legend that emerged in the 1980s and reached peak popularity in the 1990s. The legend tells of an onryō — a vengeful ghost — formed when a young woman or schoolgirl fell from a railway platform and was cut in two by an oncoming train. In most retellings she dies because of inadequate response by station staff and bystanders. Now lacking the lower half of her body, she travels on her hands or elbows at extremely high speed, dragging her bisected torso along the ground and producing a scratching sound rendered onomatopoeically as 'teke teke teke teke'. Encountering her at night, especially in train stations, school grounds, or empty streets, allegedly leads to pursuit; if she catches a victim, she severs them at the waist with a scythe or similar implement, perpetuating the cycle. Teke Teke is closely related to the older urban legend of Kashima Reiko, a girl in Hokkaidō traditionally said to have lost her legs in a railway accident; both legends share a railway-trauma origin. A Japanese horror film, 'Teketeke', was released in 2009, with a sequel the same year. The legend belongs to a broader cluster of Japanese urban-legend ghosts (kuchisake-onna, Hanako-san, aka manto) that became cultural touchstones in late-20th-century Japan.

aliases.name: テケテケ

aliases.name: Kashima Reiko
aliases.meaning: Closely related Japanese urban-legend figure of a girl whose legs were severed by a train, often treated as a precursor to the Teke Teke legend

origin: Originally a Japanese schoolyard / tabloid urban legend; widely diffused since the 2000s through Japanese horror media and English-language internet culture.

etymology.origin: Japanese onomatopoeia 'teke teke', the scratching or scuttling sound she is said to make as she pulls her body along the ground.
etymology.meaning: Approximately 'scratch-scratch' — naming the entity after the sound of her movement.
etymology.first_use: 1980s schoolyard urban legends in Japan; popularised in the 1990s in tabloids and television.

timeline.event: Teke Teke and related Kashima Reiko legends are in active oral and print circulation in Japan
timeline.significance: Anchor period of the legend's emergence

timeline.event: Japanese horror film 'Teketeke', directed by Kōji Shiraishi, is released in Japan
timeline.significance: Major film treatment that helped diffuse the legend internationally
Cements the legend in J-horror franchises
